subject: general
question: How many sections does the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 contain?
solution:
The correct answer is __**358**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023** is a significant legal document introduced to replace the colonial-era Indian Penal Code (IPC) of 1860.
 
• The BNS comprises a total of **358 sections**, which aim to modernize and restructure India's criminal justice system to meet contemporary needs.
 
• The new legislation emphasizes the principles of justice, fairness, and equality while addressing issues with the older IPC that were deemed outdated or inadequate.
 
• The **Government of India** introduced this bill as part of broader reforms in criminal laws, including changes to the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) and the Evidence Act.
 
• The BNS incorporates provisions for stricter punishments for crimes such as terrorism, organized crime, and crimes against women and children, reflecting the evolving socio-political landscape of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Purpose of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS):**

 
 
• The BNS aims to replace the outdated Indian Penal Code, ensuring that legal provisions align with **modern societal values** and international standards.
 
• It emphasizes a victim-centric approach, ensuring justice for victims of crime while safeguarding the rights of the accused.
 
• Clearer definitions of offenses and the inclusion of new categories of crimes address gaps in the previous legal framework.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Reform:**
 
 
• The IPC was drafted during the British colonial era and reflected the priorities of that time. The BNS seeks to address the **present-day needs of Indian society**.
 
• It incorporates provisions for crimes like **cybercrimes, financial frauds, and human trafficking**, which were not adequately addressed in the IPC.
 
• The legislation also aims to expedite the legal process, reducing delays in the criminal justice system.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with the Indian Penal Code (IPC):**
 
 
• The IPC had a total of **511 sections**, compared to the BNS’s **358 sections**, reflecting efforts to streamline and simplify the legal framework.
 
• The BNS eliminates provisions considered obsolete or redundant while introducing new sections for crimes relevant to modern times.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Justice Delivery:**
 
 
• The BNS promotes **alternative dispute resolution mechanisms** and community policing to reduce the burden on courts.
 
• Provisions for stricter penalties and reforms in sentencing aim to deter crimes and ensure proportional justice.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of BNS:**
 
 
• Inclusion of provisions for **gender equality** and protection of marginalized communities.
 
• Focus on reducing delays through technology-driven solutions like online filing of complaints and virtual court hearings.
 
• Enhanced safeguards against misuse of laws, ensuring a balance between enforcement and individual rights.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Introduction of the Bill:** The BNS, along with two other bills aimed at reforming criminal laws, was introduced in **August 2023** by the Union Home Minister.
 
• **Scope of Reforms:** The reforms aim to address not just substantive criminal law but also procedural aspects, ensuring a **comprehensive overhaul** of the criminal justice system.
 
• **Public Participation:** The government sought feedback from various stakeholders, including legal experts and the general public, to make the reforms inclusive and representative.
 
• **Implementation Challenges:** The transition from the IPC to the BNS requires extensive training for law enforcement agencies and judiciary members.
